The Sociological Perspective: The systematic study of human society and social behaviour
Seeing the connection between personal troubles and public issues
The patterned arrangements of relationships that shape behaviour
Viewing society as parts working together for stability
Viewing society as competition over scarce resources and power
Focusing on how people create meaning through everyday interaction
Studying large-scale social patterns and institutions
The intended and recognised purpose of a social institution
An unintended and often unrecognised consequence
A social pattern that disrupts the operation of society

Research Methods in Sociology: Hypothesis
A testable prediction about the relationship between variables
Independent variable
The factor a researcher changes or treats as the cause
Dependent variable
The outcome measured, thought to be affected by the cause
Correlation
A relationship in which two variables change together
Causation
A relationship in which one variable actually produces a change in another
Survey research
Gathering data by asking a sample a standardised set of questions
Random sample
A sample where every member of the population has an equal chance of selection
Participant observation
Studying a group by joining its everyday activities
Secondary analysis
Using data originally collected by someone else
Operational definition
A precise statement of how a concept will be measured
Reliability
Whether repeated measurement yields consistent results
Validity
Whether a measure actually captures what it claims to measure
Informed consent
Participants agreeing to research after understanding its risks
Culture and Society: Culture
The beliefs, values, behaviours, and objects shared by a group
Material culture
The physical objects a society creates and uses
Nonmaterial culture
The ideas, values, and norms a society holds
Norm
A rule or expectation guiding behaviour in a society
Folkway
A casual norm about routine or everyday behaviour
More
A norm with strong moral significance whose violation is serious
Taboo
A prohibition so strong that violation causes disgust
Value
A broad standard of what a culture considers good or desirable
Subculture
A group with distinctive patterns existing within a larger culture
Counterculture
A group whose values strongly oppose those of the wider society
Ethnocentrism
Judging another culture by the standards of one's own
Cultural relativism
Understanding a culture on its own terms
Cultural lag
Nonmaterial culture adjusting more slowly than material culture
Sapir-Whorf hypothesis
The claim that language shapes how people perceive reality
Socialization: Socialization
The lifelong process of learning a society's culture
Agent of socialization
A person or institution that teaches social expectations
Primary socialization
Early learning of basic norms, mostly within the family
Secondary socialization
Later learning of the norms of specific settings such as school
Anticipatory socialization
Practising for a role one expects to hold in the future
Resocialization
Replacing old norms and behaviours with new ones
Total institution
A setting that fully controls residents' lives, such as a prison
Looking-glass self
Cooley's idea that identity forms from how we think others see us
The I and the me
Mead's distinction between spontaneous self and socialised self
Significant other
A person whose approval strongly shapes a child's self-concept
Generalized other
The internalised expectations of society as a whole
Nature versus nurture
The debate over the relative influence of biology and environment
Feral child case
Evidence that social contact is required for normal human development
Social Structure and Interaction: A recognised social position a person occupies
A position assigned at birth or involuntarily
A position earned through effort or choice
The status that dominates how others see a person
The behaviour expected of someone holding a particular status
Tension between the demands of two different statuses
Tension among competing demands within a single status
Disengaging from a role central to one's identity
Goffman's view of social life as a theatrical performance
Public performance versus private relaxation of the role
An enduring structure meeting a basic societal need
Community based on personal ties versus society based on impersonal ties
Groups and Organizations: Two or more people who interact and share an identity
People in the same place who do not interact meaningfully
People sharing a trait but not interacting
A small, intimate, long-lasting group such as a family
A group toward which a member feels loyalty
A group toward which a member feels opposition or indifference
A group used as a standard for self-evaluation
A two-person group versus a three-person group
Conformity pressure that suppresses dissent and harms decisions
A formal organisation with hierarchy, rules, and specialisation
The tendency for organisations to concentrate power in few hands
The spread of efficiency, calculability, predictability, and control
Deviance and Social Control: Behaviour that violates a society's norms
Behaviour that violates a formally enacted law
The mechanisms a society uses to encourage conformity
An unofficial reward or punishment such as praise or ridicule
An official reward or punishment applied by an institution
Merton's idea that deviance arises when goals outpace legitimate means
Accepting cultural goals but using illegitimate means
Learning deviance through interaction with deviant others
The view that deviance results from the label society applies
An initial norm violation with little effect on self-concept
Deviance adopted as an identity after being labelled
A powerfully negative label that changes a person's identity
Discouraging crime through the threat of punishment
Social Stratification: Social stratification
The ranking of groups in a hierarchy of resources and status
Caste system
A closed stratification system based on ascribed status
Class system
An open system in which achievement can change position
Social mobility
Movement between positions in a stratification system
Intergenerational mobility
A change in status between parents and children
Intragenerational mobility
A change in status within one person's lifetime
Socioeconomic status
A composite of income, education, and occupation
Wealth versus income
Total assets owned versus money received over a period
Absolute poverty
Lacking the resources needed for survival
Relative poverty
Having far less than the standard of one's society
Poverty line
The official income threshold defining poverty
Feminization of poverty
The disproportionate concentration of poverty among women
Meritocracy
A system in which position reflects ability and effort
Davis-Moore thesis
The functionalist claim that stratification motivates skilled work
Race and Ethnicity: Race
A socially constructed category based on perceived physical traits
Ethnicity
Shared cultural heritage, language, or ancestry
Minority group
A group with less power, regardless of population size
Prejudice
A prejudgement or attitude about a group
Discrimination
Unequal treatment of people based on group membership
Institutional discrimination
Bias built into the normal operation of organisations
Stereotype
An oversimplified generalisation applied to a whole group
Scapegoat theory
Blaming a vulnerable group for one's own frustrations
Assimilation
A minority group adopting the dominant culture
Pluralism
Distinct groups coexisting with equal standing
Segregation
The physical and social separation of groups
Genocide
The systematic annihilation of a group of people
Self-fulfilling prophecy
A false expectation producing the behaviour that confirms it
Gender and Age: Sex
Biological characteristics distinguishing male and female
Gender
The social and cultural meanings attached to sex
Gender role
Society's expectations about how each gender should behave
Gender socialization
Learning the expectations attached to one's gender
Sexism
Prejudice or discrimination based on gender
Glass ceiling
An invisible barrier limiting advancement of qualified women
Second shift
Unpaid household work performed after paid employment
Gender pay gap
The average earnings difference between men and women
Ageism
Prejudice or discrimination based on age
Life course
The socially defined stages people pass through with age
Graying of society
The rising share of older people in a population
Disengagement theory
The view that older adults gradually withdraw from roles
Activity theory
The view that staying active supports wellbeing in later life
Family and Education: Family
A social institution uniting people in cooperative groups to care for members
Nuclear family
Parents and their children living as one unit
Extended family
A household including relatives beyond the nuclear core
Family of orientation
The family a person is born into
Family of procreation
The family a person forms as an adult
Monogamy and polygamy
Marriage to one partner versus more than one
Endogamy and exogamy
Marrying within one's group versus outside it
Blended family
A family formed when partners with existing children unite
Education
The social institution transmitting knowledge and skills
Hidden curriculum
The unstated lessons in values and behaviour taught by schools
Tracking
Sorting students into groups by perceived ability
Credentialism
Requiring degrees for jobs that may not need them
Cultural capital
Knowledge and tastes that provide social advantage
Social Change and Movements: Social change
Transformation in culture and social institutions over time
Modernization
The shift from traditional to industrial and urban society
Collective behaviour
Spontaneous activity by a large number of people
Crowd
A temporary gathering of people sharing a focus
Mass hysteria
Widespread anxiety spreading rapidly through a population
Social movement
Organised activity encouraging or discouraging social change
Reform movement
A movement seeking limited change within the existing system
Revolutionary movement
A movement seeking to replace the existing system
Resource mobilization theory
The view that movements succeed by acquiring resources
Relative deprivation
Feeling worse off compared with a reference group
Globalization
The increasing interconnection of economies and cultures worldwide
Urbanization
The concentration of population in cities
Demographic transition
The shift from high to low birth and death rates with development
